Also ISVs and partners building AutoML solutions on OpenShift AI.
Business justification: AutoML market projected to reach $12.8B by 2030; tabular data represents 70%+ of enterprise ML use cases. Supporting AutoGluon natively attracts ease-of-use-focused users and increases platform adoption. Eliminates 2-4 hours of manual configuration per model deployment. Official Red Hat support removes enterprise adoption risk and unlocks customers who cannot use unsupported custom runtimes.
User problem: Today, deploying an AutoGluon model requires users to manually obtain a KServe container image, navigate to Settings → Serving runtimes, write or paste complex ServingRuntime YAML requiring knowledge of KServe specs, API protocols, and resource configuration. The resulting custom runtime is explicitly marked as unsupported by Red Hat. This creates a massive barrier for non-ML-expert users (citizen data scientists, data analysts) who chose AutoML precisely because training was easy, but now face Kubernetes-level complexity at deployment time. Unlike vLLM, OpenVINO, and Triton, there is no streamlined one-click deployment experience for AutoGluon.
Scope: Single focused need — adding AutoGluon as a pre-configured, officially supported serving runtime in the OpenShift AI dashboard. Initial GA scope covers tabular models (regression, binary/multiclass classification, time series forecasting), CSV input/JSON output, single-model serving (KServe-based), and REST API protocol.
Success criteria: AutoGluon appears in the runtime selection dropdown alongside vLLM, OpenVINO, and Triton. Users can deploy an AutoGluon TabularPredictor model by selecting AutoGluon from the dropdown, specifying a model location, and clicking Deploy — no YAML authoring required. A Red Hat-verified container image is published and maintained. AutoGluon runtime is listed in the Red Hat OpenShift AI Supported Configurations document and included in Red Hat support scope. Official documentation including deployment guide, examples, API reference, and troubleshooting is available. However, as the pipeline itself correctly notes, there are **no named customer accounts with specific revenue impact**. The justification is segment-level and market-level, not deal-level. The pipeline correctly self-assessed this as 1/2 and even provided guidance on what would elevate it ("Customer X in financial services blocked until we support AutoGluon"). **Score of 1/2 is accurate and well-calibrated.**

### Open to HOW (Pipeline score: 2/2)
The RFE describes user-facing needs (dashboard runtime picker, REST API, container image) without prescribing internal architecture. References to KServe are platform vocabulary — established technology in the RHOAI ecosystem. The RFE doesn't mandate specific internal implementation choices. The feasibility review discusses KServe patterns and technical details, but those are in the review/feasibility documents, not the RFE itself. ### Not a Task (Pipeline score: 2/2)
The RFE describes a clear business need addressing market opportunity and adoption friction. It's framed as enabling a customer segment currently blocked from using RHOAI for AutoGluon workloads. It references specific overlays, JIRAs, and technical details. The strategy considerations are practical and actionable.

### Review Quality
The review file is well-structured with clear criterion-by-criterion scoring, specific notes, and actionable improvement suggestions. The needs_attention flag and reason are appropriate (registry image fix, CVE SLAs).

### Minor Issues
1. The "Open Questions" at the end of the RFE include "Should the initial release support only CPU inference, or should GPU serving also be included?" — but the feasibility review and scope section already establish CPU-only for GA. This is a minor inconsistency but not significant.

3. The success criteria include "At least 2 named customers or partners publicly reference using native AutoGluon runtime on RHOAI within 6 months" — this is good but aspirational rather than evidence-based.

### Overall Assessment
This is a high-quality RFE with strong articulation of the business need, clear user scenarios, well-defined scope, and appropriate technical context. The pipeline's self-scoring is accurate — the only deduction (WHY: 1/2) is correctly identified and justified. The feasibility review adds significant value with thorough technical analysis.
